clue.text: Heavenly ale to be drunk outside that place

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters split and go round the other piece
drunk suggests the letters of ale are reeling about into a new order

parts.note: that place means there

explanation.surface: Someone finds the beer divine, waiting to be drunk over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns ALE into EAL, and 'outside' splits it as E...AL round THERE; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate and otherworldly seems to belong to the heavens.

clue.text: Rooms in which char is often seen

definitions.text: Rooms in which char is often seen

parts.words: Rooms in which char is often seen
parts.note: char is British slang for tea, not a cleaning woman; these are rooms where the drink is served

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman is regularly found in certain rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a char is a cleaning woman, which the surface suggests; in slang char is also tea, the drink served here.
explanation.definitionFit: A café serving cups of the brew is a set of rooms where char, slang for the drink, is always seen.

clue.text: After getting in fellows start to tingle with sense of delight

parts.note: getting in, read as a noun, is an entrance, a way or act of entering
fellows are men

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of tingle is used

explanation.surface: Once inside, the men begin to tingle with pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'with' are links; 'getting in' looks like a verb but is the noun ENTRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of rapture or enchantment is a feeling of delight.

clue.text: After one's gone over the paper, mistakes can be rectified

definitions.text: After one's gone over the paper, mistakes can be rectified

parts.words: After one's gone over the paper, mistakes can be rectified
parts.note: reads like a teacher marking a script, but describes a tool rubbed across the paper to remove pencil errors

explanation.surface: Once someone has checked the exam script, errors can be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber, the tool for removing pencil marks, is passed over paper to undo mistakes.

clue.text: Story-teller in bar getting sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a bar is a rail

explanation.surface: A raconteur at the pub is being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story-teller' looks like an author but means someone who tells lies; 'in' is a link. 'getting sent up' turns RAIL round to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for telling fibs, so a teller of them is a fibber.

clue.text: What is there in a vacuum? Never mind!

definitions.text: What is there in a vacuum?
definitions.meaning: a vacuum is space holding no substance, nothing physical at all
an exclamation brushing something aside as unimportant

explanation.surface: A science question followed by a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum contains zero physical substance; the same phrase also dismisses something as unimportant, like 'forget it'.

clue.text: Man in middle of room keeping dry

indicators.note: keeping says the central letters hold the other piece between them
middle of takes the central letters of the word room, here two of them

parts.note: dry means teetotal, abbreviated TT

explanation.surface: A man stands in the centre of a room, keeping off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives OO, the centre pair of ROOM; 'keeping' puts TT between the two O's. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A German given name for a male, so it fits a generic man.

clue.text: Keep quiet having reticence

parts.note: P is short for piano, quiet in music
reticence is reserve

explanation.surface: Stay silent and hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to maintain or save something from loss.

clue.text: I perform subsequently as a false worshipper

parts.note: to perform is to do
subsequently means later

explanation.surface: Someone says they will play the part of a heathen later on.
explanation.definitionFit: One who worships idols adores false gods.

clue.text: Stupid duke at the rear

parts.note: aft means at the back, in nautical use

explanation.surface: A foolish duke brings up the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for silly or foolish.

clue.text: Displaced tribes to be put in them? One has qualms

definitions.text: Displaced tribes to be put in them?
definitions.meaning: land set aside for native peoples moved off their territory, as in North America

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy about uprooting peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Land reserved for displaced peoples, and doubts or misgivings, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Old south American coming down from mountain perhaps getting very hot

parts.note: Incan describes the old ruling people of Peru, used here as a noun for one of them
coming down a mountain is a descent; perhaps flags it as one example

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian overheats on the way down a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing white with intense heat describes a material becoming extremely hot.

clue.text: Athlete at Oxford possibly not the winner

parts.note: a runner is a kind of athlete
to be up is to be in residence at a university, Oxford being one example

explanation.surface: An Oxford sportsman may not have won.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-placed finisher is by definition not the champion.

clue.text: Academic has extra zero put in — it satisfies the mathematicians

indicators.note: put in says the nought is placed inside the academic

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A professor adds another nought, to the delight of number crunchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has extra' just says the professor gains a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians demand a rigorous demonstration before accepting a theorem.

clue.text: Heart examiner giving an encouraging sign?

definitions.meaning: slang for the heart, which beats like a clock
one who marks answers right with a check mark, a playful coinage

explanation.surface: A cardiologist offers some hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for the heart, and whimsically one who puts check marks on work.

clue.text: Pool contributing to summer entertainment

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lake features in some summer fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lake or pond is a pool of water.

clue.text: Creative type who could be 'crotchety'?

parts.note: a crotchet is a quarter note in music, so crotchety jokingly means full of crotchets rather than bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Artistic people may be grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer or player works with crotchets, the British term for quarter notes.

clue.text: Relationship taking a little woman to Abraham's place

parts.note: Mo is a short (little) form of women's names such as Maureen
Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's home city in Genesis

explanation.surface: A love affair takes a girl to Abraham's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'to' are links. Ur is the Mesopotamian city Abraham left in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, usually a secret one, is a romantic relationship.

clue.text: Opponent no longer with us — difficult daughter

parts.note: anti, as a noun, is someone opposed
gone means dead or departed

explanation.surface: A dead rival's daughter was trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy Oedipus's defiant daughter disobeys Creon to bury her brother.

clue.text: Pleasant church to the east of the province

indicators.note: in an across clue, to the east of puts church on the right of the province

parts.note: the Province is Northern Ireland, NI
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pleasant church lies east of the province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the province' is the usual name for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and pleasant are close synonyms.

clue.text: Scarves ingeniously used to conceal ecstasy and crack

indicators.note: to conceal says the rearranged letters hide the other piece within them
ingeniously suggests the letters of Scarves are cleverly rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Clever use of scarves to hide drugs and a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingeniously' rearranges SCARVES to CRVASSE, and 'to conceal' puts E inside it after the R; 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep fissure in glacier ice is a crack.

clue.text: Quiet is returning — sober period?

indicators.note: returning means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the forty days of Christian fasting and abstinence

explanation.surface: Is it peaceful when one gives up drink for a spell?
explanation.definitionFit: Making no sound is being quiet.

clue.text: Security device broken to make stan free

indicators.note: broken says the letters of stan free are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lock is broken to set someone called Stan free.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp, bolt or catch secures things, so it is a security device.

clue.text: Son a bit chilly side gets hot in his classrooms etc

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Son a bit chilly side gets hot in his classrooms etc (6)': S + COOL with H inside gives SCHOOL, but 'side' and 'his' have no job and no source gives the clue as printed; it appears garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Son a bit chilly side gets hot in his classrooms etc

clue.text: Chap tragic or silly in respect of maps

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the three words are scrambled foolishly

explanation.surface: A man is tragic, or foolish, about maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to mapmaking describes anything to do with charts of land.

clue.text: Rugby street shows sign of decay

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A rugby club's street shows signs of dilapidation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosion on iron is a visible mark of deterioration.

clue.text: A biblical place with a distinctive character

parts.note: Ur is the Mesopotamian city named in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible town has something special about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atmosphere or quality surrounding a person or place gives it distinctive character.

clue.text: Relief brought by medicine as expected

indicators.note: brought by suggests the answer is carried along within the next words

explanation.surface: Medicine gave the expected relief.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is medicinE AS Expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief from pain or worry is comfort, a release.

clue.text: Some crass, ignorant person making legal transfer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some foolish, uninformed person signs over property.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who hands over a right or property to another under law.

clue.text: A good set of piglets brilliantly attractive

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together

explanation.surface: A fine litter of piglets looks dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling, shining things catch the eye, so they are brilliantly attractive.
